root_cause: Not a bug. The maintainer (willmcgugan) restyled Markdown rendering to taste: new colors in DEFAULT_STYLES, h1 no longer boxed in a Panel, headings justified per level, hr drawn with '-' plus a blank line, tables with a new box style and theme styles. The statement ('Update to markdown styles / Updates to Markdown styling') gives none of these choices.
best_solution: rich/default_styles.py: bullet=Style(bold=True), number=Style(color='cyan'), hr=Style(dim=True), h1=bold+underline, h2=magenta+underline, h3=magenta+bold, h4=magenta+italic, h5=italic, h6=dim; add 'markdown.table.border'=Style(color='cyan') and 'markdown.table.header'=Style(color='cyan', bold=False). rich/markdown.py: remove the Panel import; add a HeadingFormat dataclass; add Heading.LEVEL_ALIGN (h1 center, h2-h6 left); Heading.__rich_console__ now yields self.text.copy() with the justify taken from LEVEL_ALIGN (no Panel for h1, no blank line before h2); HorizontalRule yields Rule(style=style, characters='-') and then Text(); TableElement builds Table(box=box.SIMPLE, pad_edge=False, style='markdown.table.border', show_edge=True, collapse_padding=True) and stylizes a copy of each header cell with 'markdown.table.header'. None of these values can be worked out from the statement. They are aesthetic choices that only the hidden expected-output strings encode.
hidden_test_demands: Byte-exact ANSI snapshots: tests/test_markdown.py::test_markdown_render, test_markdown_table, test_inline_styles_in_table, test_inline_styles_with_justification, test_partial_table (expected e.g. '\n\x1b[36m               \x1b[0m\n\x1b[36m \x1b[0m\x1b[36mSimple\x1b[0m\x1b[1m \x1b[0m... ───────────── ...'), and tests/test_markdown_no_hyperlinks.py::test_markdown_render. Every color code, box character (SIMPLE '─' rather than SIMPLE_HEAVY '━'), padding and justification has to match exactly. tests/_card_render.py was also regenerated.
locating_signals: 'markdown styles' leads to rich/markdown.py and the markdown.* entries in rich/default_styles.py, so finding the files is easy. The statement names no function, style key or target value.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass=false), with 6 of 8 markdown tests failing each time. v4, v6 and v7 produced empty patches (0 chars after 15-32 calls). v8 (304s, 41 calls) made a 1022-char guess in default_styles.py only: it removed bgcolor from markdown.code and markdown.code_block, made block_quote bright_black, and added duplicate link and link_url keys. It left alone the keys the gold changed (bullet, number, hr, h1-h6) and made no markdown.py changes (Panel h1, hr characters, table box and styles), so every snapshot still mismatched.
generalizable_lesson: Check whether the task can be solved before spending the budget. If the statement is a bare PR title or body with no concrete values, and the area is snapshot-tested (ANSI/SVG/golden strings), the hidden tests encode arbitrary exact output that cannot be inferred. Don't burn many calls on it: make a small, plausible, self-consistent edit (or none) and move on to other tasks. Also, when an agent does change styles, it should change existing keys rather than add duplicate dict keys.
acceptable_alternatives: None in practice. Any different color, box or justification choice breaks the byte-exact snapshots.
